subject: late appearance of ggplots from for loop

messages.author: b878b27022ed7fbd
messages.subject: late appearance of ggplots from for loop
parts:
Hi! I'm trying to generate a bunch of plots with some supporting text for each. I'm doing it in a for loop. Because I need to have other text, which could be arbitrarily long, pulled in before and after each plot, I can't really use plot text or faceting for this. The problem I'm having is that the first plot comes out where the second plot should be, and so on. Here's a very simple illustration:

```{r demo, results='asis', echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
data <- data.frame(rnorm(1000),rep(letters, len=1000))
names(data) <- c("value","category")
for (i in 1:6) {
  cat(paste("#",LETTERS[i],"\n"))
  print(ggplot(subset(data,category==letters[i]), aes(x=value)) + geom_histogram())
  cat("\n")
}
```

This yields results that look like this when rendered in the browser:

A
B
[plot a]
C
[plot b]
D
[plot c]
E
[plot d]
F
[plot e]
[plot f]

I really want [plot a] to appear right after A. I've tried things like Sys.sleep(0) or dev.flush() after the print(), just because I was trying anything I could find. Am I missing a chunk option I ought to have in there or something? How can this be fixed?

Thanks,


- Aaron

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] late appearance of ggplots from for loop
parts:
Hi:

Take out the "\n" in the first cat() call within the loop. That seemed
to work for me.

HTH,
Dennis

https://gist.github.com/3145751

On Wed, Aug 8, 2012 at 8:40 PM, Ryan Mears <rme...@gmail.com> wrote:
I had the same problem with knitr, ggplot and LaTeX. A loop produced delayed figures.
My next approach was knitting over a loop with a child document.
http://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/63941/looping-a-code-chunk-in-latex
This attempt produced a correct Tex document that would not evaluate to pdf.
Next, I will try to Brew a recursive loop. http://learnr.wordpress.com/2009/09/09/brew-creating-repetitive-reports/
However, I have had trouble integrating this with knitr.

I'm interested in solving my problem of using recursion to produce dynamic reports, but part of my interest is to better understand knitr.
-Ryan
